tonight.headline: Down 22.6 before you've played, and Friday went your way
body: Christian Watson's 22.6 on Thursday is all Footballers have. ESPN projects you 134.4 to their 128.6 and gives you 53%. Your lineup as set is the projection lineup.

Friday's reports mostly helped. Warren and Coker are both questionable but expected to play. Their tight end Brock Bowers didn't practise Friday and needs a Sunday workout. Nothing to do today; the two cards below are Sunday-morning fallbacks only.

case.label: Their weak spots
case.body: Bowers (knee) didn't practise Friday. The Raiders plan a workout before Sunday to decide on his season debut (Audacy/WWL). Footballers carry no second tight end. Caleb Williams is doubtful, so they start Stafford (Heavy, 25 Sep).

case.label: Your weak spots
case.body: Warren (shoulder) was limited all week, but Pittsburgh's running backs coach says they expect him to play, and Dowdle is ruled out (Still Curtain). Coker (ankle) was limited Friday after missing Thursday (Panthers.com); DraftSharks list him as expected to play.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker or Warren inactive at about 09:30 Sunday and the fallback not used. Either one scores zero, and you drop to roughly a coin flip.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN league file · Audacy/WWL · Heavy · Still Curtain · Panthers.com · DraftSharks

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Check Sunday inactives about 09:30 Mexico City; all three play at 11:00
doFirst.title: Only if Coker is inactive: start McLaurin in the flex
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Don't do this today. Swap only, nothing dropped. Coker is questionable but expected to play.

case.label: Friday's report
case.body: Coker was limited Friday after sitting out Thursday, and is listed questionable (Panthers.com, NBC Sports). DraftSharks call him expected to play. Xavier Legette is also questionable, so Carolina may be thin at receiver either way.

case.label: Why McLaurin, not Boston
case.body: McLaurin projects 11.8 and drew 9 targets in Week 2. Boston projects 11.3 and drew 7 (week archive). That's close on both, so I'm taking the projection and writing no thesis. McLaurin gets Seattle, who have allowed the fewest WR points (footballdb), with Mariota throwing.

case.label: No timing trap
case.body: Coker, McLaurin and Boston all kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City. The 07:00 Sunday brief runs before inactives, so check them yourself.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is active on Sunday. The card then never fires and costs nothing.

action.label: Start McLaurin · bench Coker (only if Coker is inactive)

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only. Check Sunday inactives about 09:30 Mexico City; both play at 11:00
doFirst.title: Only if Warren is inactive: start Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed, and less likely than this morning. Friday didn't rule Warren out. Nothing is dropped.

case.label: Friday's report
case.body: Warren was limited again Friday and is questionable. Running backs coach Ramon Chinyoung Sr. said the Steelers expect him to play. Rico Dowdle is ruled out, so if Warren plays the backfield is his, with Travis Homer rotating (Still Curtain).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Warren projects 15.0 to Tuten's 11.0. Swapping on a questionable tag throws away four points.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Warren is active on Sunday. The card then never fires. This morning's condition (OUT or DOUBTFUL on Friday) did not fire.

action.label: Start Tuten · bench Warren (only if Warren is inactive)

whatWentWrong.title: Coker's ankle is still the open question
whatWentWrong.lead: Limited Friday after missing Thursday, and questionable. On Thursday morning a brief said his availability wasn't in doubt. The first card is the fix.

case.label: What happened
case.body: He has played through the ankle since Week 1. Thursday was the first practice he missed; Friday he was back, limited (Panthers.com).

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing today. The flex has a same-kickoff fallback in McLaurin.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker plays Sunday and draws his usual 8-9 targets. Then Thursday was maintenance, not a setback.

worthALook.name: Evan McPherson
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison, and hold is now easy.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 3 board has McPherson K1, Trey Smack K2 and your Pineiro K3. That settles this morning's worry, which rested on boards that had Pineiro 15th-17th.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep, so moving him would be the second change to that seat in a week, for no gain.

case.label: When to act
case.body: 30 September, when the churn window closes, and only if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson finishes top five.

worthALook.name: Lions D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison. Hold the Vikings.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN has the Lions 7.8 to the Vikings' 7.7. The Lions are on waivers until Sunday 01:00 Mexico City after you dropped them today. The Vikings face Tampa Bay, whose offence has given defences the 30th-most points (footballdb). The Lions face a Jets offence that has given up the 7th-fewest.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: A 0.1 gap isn't a reason to touch a seat that has changed hands three times since 23 Sep.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If the Vikings finish outside the top fifteen while the Lions finish top five, revisit when the week rolls.

doNotChase.lead: The market is right about him, and it doesn't matter here.

case.label: The role
case.body: Houston ruled Nico Collins out again on Friday (NBC Sports), which leaves more targets for Schultz.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem has one tight-end slot, and Likely holds it. The flex takes RB/WR only, so a second tight end scores you zero.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely appearing on a Giants injury report. He's not on this week's.

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: Carried from this morning: a second tight end has no seat.

case.label: The fact
case.body: This morning's reporting had Pitts at 1.5 PPR in Thursday's 35-14 win at Green Bay while Bijan Robinson ran for 194 (Yahoo). I didn't re-search Pitts this run.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One tight-end slot, held by Likely. The flex is RB/WR only.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely getting hurt. Separately, the log grades the decline WRONG if Pitts outscores Likely in two of the next three weeks.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest movable players, and nobody clears either. Two weeks of data is a thin sample, but the tool's answer stands and I didn't go looking for a reason to disagree.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second tight end (23 Sep)
settled.result: Pitts scored 1.5 on Thursday with Penix back. The quarterback risk was never the reason.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Dart is on IR, Winston starts, and Likely led the Giants in Week 2 targets (10, week archive). The target clause is graded after Sunday.
